LESSON: READING 12.2.1 INTENSIVE READING- COMPREHENSION

Grade: Grade 7
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 12
Topic 12.2: Reading 12.2.1 Intensive Reading- Comprehension
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Reading 12.2.1 Intensive Reading- Comprehension, part of Strand 12 in Grade 7 ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: How can we tell the meaning of words and phrases in a text?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. identify the main ideas in a text,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading 12.2.1 Intensive Reading- Comprehension in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. use contextual clues to infer the meaning of words in a text,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading 12.2.1 Intensive Reading- Comprehension in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. describe characters, ideas, or events in a text,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading 12.2.1 Intensive Reading- Comprehension in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. appreciate the importance of reading comprehension in lifelong learning.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading 12.2.1 Intensive Reading- Comprehension in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. identify the main ideas in a text,

   Reading 12.2.1 Intensive Reading- Comprehension helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

B. use contextual clues to infer the meaning of words in a text,

   Reading 12.2.1 Intensive Reading- Comprehension helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

C. describe characters, ideas, or events in a text,

   Reading 12.2.1 Intensive Reading- Comprehension helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

D. appreciate the importance of reading comprehension in lifelong learning.

   Reading 12.2.1 Intensive Reading- Comprehension helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

E. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. download and share texts with mental images from the texts and draw conclusions,

2. read a passage individually, and identify keywords in the passage,

3. infer the meaning of words using contextual clues,

4. choose descriptive parts of the passage on traditional fashion and share the vivid images created in their mind,

5. role-play the characters and events in the text,

6. use contextual clues to decipher the meaning of words,

7. answer questions based on the passage,

8. give an appropriate title to a story or passage.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. download and share texts with mental images from the texts and draw conclusions,
2. read a passage individually, and identify keywords in the passage,
3. infer the meaning of words using contextual clues,
4. choose descriptive parts of the passage on traditional fashion and share the vivid images created in their mind,
5. role-play the characters and events in the text,
6. use contextual clues to decipher the meaning of words,
7. answer questions based on the passage,
8. give an appropriate title to a story or passage.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Reading 12.2.1 Intensive Reading- Comprehension together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Critical thinking: It is enhanced as the learner solves simple problems as they answer questions based on the passage and

give an appropriate title to the passage.

• Imagination: It is developed as the learner role plays the characters and events in the text.

Values:
Unity is developed when the learner displays a team spirit while collaborating with peers to role play characters and events

in a text.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Analytical thinking is enhanced when the learner infers the meaning of words using contextual clues.

Link to other Learning Areas:

The learner relates the skills of making inferences and visualising when reading texts in Kiswahili.

SECTION 6: SUMMARY

Main points to remember:

1. identify the main ideas in a text,
2. use contextual clues to infer the meaning of words in a text,
3. describe characters, ideas, or events in a text,
4. appreciate the importance of reading comprehension in lifelong learning.

Remember the key question: How can we tell the meaning of words and phrases in a text?
